Retrieved 2026-07-20 via Exa search highlights. (UK DOMESTIC lead — flagged for UK team, not GEO edition.)

Andy Burnham becomes UK PM today (Monday 20 July 2026), succeeding Keir Starmer. Starmer to deliver final address to the nation as PM this morning; Burnham his first, on the steps of No 10. Both travel to Buckingham Palace: Charles III first offered Starmer's resignation, then asks Burnham to form a government ("kissing hands").
Starmer announced 22 June he would step down, four days after Burnham won a Westminster seat (Makerfield by-election). Triggered a one-candidate race: 379 Labour MPs nominated the former Greater Manchester mayor; Burnham became Labour leader on Friday (17 July). Wes Streeting backed Burnham.
Burnham will be the UK's SEVENTH prime minister since 2016 (in ~10 years). In his first speech as leader he said the UK had "turned its back on the working class." Starmer leaves as shortest-serving Labour PM in history (took office 5 July 2024).

QUOTE - Keir Starmer (resignation address, via NPR): "Every prime minister knows when they take up the torch, that the day will come when they have to pass it on. That day has come for me. This is the end of my political journey."

GEO relevance: new PM inherits the Hormuz crisis mid-escalation — UK/France lead the multinational reassurance mission (RFA Lyme Bay minehunting mothership, HMS Dragon) to reopen the Strait; Starmer had called for "unrestricted freedom of navigation" and warned of winter energy-bill impact.
